17:00:12 KST

Evidence of earliest silkworm farming outside China found, upending Silk Road timeline
4,000-year-old cocoons found in Uzbekistan likely made their way to the region 2,000 years before the Silk Road even existed
It may not be the most majestic creature on our beautiful planet, but the humble silkworm deserves a place alongside horses, cattle, cats, and dogs due to its profound impact on human civilisation.
The luxurious fabric spun from the silkworm’s natural secretion ignited the creation of a vast global trade network, connecting Asia with the Mediterranean. This network became a catalyst for transformative exchanges of goods, ideas, and technologies across continents, significantly shaping the course of world history.
However, the history of silk predates the Silk Road, with archaeological excavations suggesting its origins lie within the Yangshao culture (5000 BC–3000 BC) during Neolithic China.
Now, a new study from Washington University in St. Louis suggests that the silkworm cocoons left China far earlier than previously thought.
The researchers, whose work was published in the peer-reviewed scientific journal Science Advances, discovered three silkworm cocoons along the Surkhan-Darya River, which flows across southeast Uzbekistan between Tajikistan and Afghanistan.
The scientists estimated that these cocoons are about 4,000 years old, indicating they were transferred to Central Asia around 2,000 years before the traditional narrative of the luxurious garb’s spread along the Silk Road.
Xinyi Liu, a professor of archaeology at Washington University and lead author for the study, stated that the silkworm artefact in question is the oldest known reliable example of a silkworm cocoon.

From Lucerne to La Catedral glory: the global rise of a Swiss wrestling icon
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
08:00:00 UTC
17:00:00 KST

From Lucerne to La Catedral glory: the global rise of a Swiss wrestling icon
Lucerne native Claudio Castagnoli has made his name internationally in a sport that gets little attention in Switzerland: wrestling. With a wrestling persona as a wealthy Swiss banker, he won some of the most prestigious titles in the US and tells Swissinfo how he fell in love with the scene in Mexico.
Professional wrestling and Switzerland are not the most intuitive of pairings. The North American version, as made famous by World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE), has never been particularly popular in Switzerland, and unlike France, Germany or the United Kingdom, it lacks a deep tradition of independent “promotions”, the companies that organise and produce the shows.
But anyone who has been following wrestling for the last couple decades probably knows the name of a colossal Lucerne native: Claudio Castagnoli (or Cesaro).
He is a multi-time champion in tag matches (involving two-wrestler teams) in the 2000s indies, the independent promotions that mushroomed at the beginning of the century, revolutionising the sport. He is a trios (three-wrestler teams) champion in All Elite Wrestling (AEW), WWE United States Champion, and world champion in Ring of Honor (ROH), Pro-Wrestling Guerrilla (PWG), Westside Xtreme Wrestling, and Mexico’s Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre.
Castagnoli’s career is storied, but it wasn’t easy getting there while holding a Swiss passport.
A stairway to wrestling
Always an active kid, Castagnoli started playing tennis as a six-year-old, before switching to football, where he had a very successful run as the main striker for his local squad, and developed his initial fandom for FC Luzern.
As Claudio continued to grow, signs of his prominent stature and athletic prowess became more and more noticeable, and with this came a newfound passion for basketball, which he followed religiously through broadcast news teletexts the morning after the US primetime NBA games. He was selected for regional teams, but never embarked seriously on this path, as the allure of pro-wrestling had already made its way into his life by his late teens.
“I was a fan like everybody else, and I saw a guy from Switzerland who actually wrestled: Siegmeister Rapo,” Castagnoli, 45, says. “He wrestled in Germany and a little bit in the US. I saw he trained somewhere in Zurich, just in a gym on mats. So I went there, tried it out, liked it, and started travelling with him to Germany. I started doing more and more, and with another guy from Switzerland we formed the tag team Swiss Money Holding. It was just two rich Swiss bankers travelling to Germany as wrestlers. In those days, the more over-the-top the character the better. So we took something stereotypical like a Swiss banker and had a blast being obnoxious and provocative.”
Enter the dragon
European success puts wrestlers in a predicament: the world’s top promotions are in the US, Japan and Mexico. Castagnoli decided to try the US first, breaking out as the wrestling world was undergoing a transition. WWE had absorbed its biggest rival, creating a monopoly that inadvertently pushed fans towards the independent boom of the mid-2000s.
Cult promotions such as ROH and PWG gained traction with their presentation, and blogs and peer-to-peer networks allowed a new generation of Western wrestlers and fans access to the Japanese and Mexican styles.
“Back in the old days we traded video cassettes,” Castagnoli says. “I discovered other American wrestling like Extreme Championship Wrestling, Japanese stuff, and then later lucha libre [Mexican professional wrestling]. I fell in love with it. I learnt fairly early on that every promotion has different rules, preferences and audiences. The better you are at adjusting your style, the better reactions you get. The US is different from Germany; Mexico is different from Japan.”
After an illustrious run in Chikara and ROH, Castagnoli began getting more prominent bookings in singles competition, where he got to showcase his superhuman strength – which would earn him the nickname of Swiss Superman. He also established feuds with cult favourites such as Eddie Kingston and Nigel McGuinness and developed a villainous persona that went on to exalt his “very European background, superior intellect and sense of fashion”.
“It was crazy looking back at the talent in ROH at that time,” he says. “We were all just trying to prove a point. Testing yourself against people better than you from different backgrounds helps you figure out how to improve. Back in the day with ROH, PWG, NOAH, New Japan, All Japan… you had to fight to get in. To get better, you have to get the reps,” he says, referring to ring performances.
Cesaro rises
Despite some unfruitful try-outs in the mid-2000s, Castagnoli finally became a full-time roster member of WWE in 2012 and stayed with the company for a decade under the ring name Cesaro. There, he became a staple of the promotion’s tag division and had critically acclaimed matches with stars such as Sami Zayn, John Cena and Sheamus; his hard-hitting European style made him a fan favourite, respected by peers and legends alike (Stone Cold Steve Austin was a fan).
However, WWE’s senior executives never committed to placing him constantly on the “upper cards” – the most prestigious positions on its roster – fearing his “wrestler’s wrestler” style wouldn’t fit their entertainment-focused product.
When AEW, a new promotion built on showcasing independent talent and styles rarely seen on US television, came calling, Castagnoli made an intuitive move, integrating himself into one of their most prominent factions, the Death Riders. Then, AEW broke stigmas further by partnering with Japan’s New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW) and Mexico’s CMLL.
“For a long time, people saw one thing and thought ‘that is it’,” Castagnoli says. “Now they have a chance to see more [forms of wrestling]. That’s the beauty of it. Everybody has their own way, and if you mix it, you get something great. [In AEW] Blue Panther can come on American television and wrestle his style. Japanese or Mexican wrestlers can come on television and speak how they would speak, and it connects differently than if you tell them how to do it. If they can just do it their way, it works.”
Mad scientists and monsters
AEW’s partnerships also gave Castagnoli a moment of personal closure. His relationship to lucha libre ran deeper than ambition. At Chikara, his mentor, Skayde, had taught him the fundamentals of the lucha style, and before that, he loved the infamous B-movies where Blue Demon, Mil Máscaras and Santo battled mad scientists and monsters.
In the mid-2000s, before his breakout at ROH, Castagnoli spent a month in Mexico City trying to get under the bright lights of Arena Mexico, the home of CMLL. It didn’t work out. Twenty years later, Castagnoli not only got to headline the Friday night events at the mythical venue in Colonia Doctores but did so as their World Heavyweight Champion, and as the first dual contract for an AEW-signed talent in Mexico.
    
        External Content    
    
            
“It was a great honour and a cool full-circle moment,” he says. “Arena Mexico is ‘La Catedral’, and you feel it. There’s no place in the world like it. You feel what it means to the people. You feel what it means to walk down those steps and step into that ring because so many legends have done it before you. In Mexico City, you walk around and there’s lucha merchandise everywhere. That level of cultural impact is amazing – and I got to be a part of it.”
Castagnoli held the CMLL World Heavyweight Championship for 112 days, ultimately losing it to Hechicero at one of Mexico’s biggest lucha events: Homenaje A Dos Leyendas. Defeat didn’t diminish the achievement: his reign was affectionately remembered by Mexican fans and media. The Swiss Superman continues to wrestle weekly on AEW and CMLL.
“Years ago, I never thought this was gonna happen,” he says. “I wanted to be a professional wrestler, that was the goal. It was never about being a champion. Now I just try to be as good as I can and see what happens. I got to wrestle at the Tokyo Dome, and then at La Catedral. I won the World Heavyweight Championship and became the first guy with a double contract. It was humbling. I’m still trying to put in the work, still trying to wrestle as good as I can, and it keeps showing me that I still need to be at the top of my game. I’m also just trying to have fun and show the world how cool, fun, and interesting professional wrestling can be.”

- UFORCE is promoting Ukrainian Magura drone strikes in Crimea ahead of a Pentagon prize challenge for drone-launching naval vessels.
- GUR confirmed strikes on two S-400 launchers, an Orion antenna, and a Pantsir-S1 system worth roughly $15 million.
UFORCE, the London-headquartered maker of Ukraine’s Magura naval drones, is touting a series of Ukrainian strikes on Russian air defenses in Crimea as evidence for its pitch to the Pentagon, days before the deadline for a Defense Innovation Unit prize challenge seeking naval drones that can launch their own aircraft.
Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence agency, GUR, said its Group 13 special operations unit destroyed or damaged Russian equipment in occupied Crimea in early August using Magura naval drones to carry smaller FPV drones toward the coast before launching them at targets on land. GUR said the unit hit two launchers from a Russian S-400 “Triumf” air defense battery and an antenna used to control “Orion” drones. In a separate strike the same week, GUR said Group 13 destroyed a Pantsir-S1 air defense system valued at roughly $15 million, along with a military crane. GUR’s own public statements put the total cost to Russian forces at tens of millions of dollars, without giving a more precise figure.
UFORCE said the value of destroyed equipment topped $80 million, a figure not confirmed in GUR’s own public statements.
“From now on, our Maguras threaten the Russian occupiers on land as well, a fundamental shift in the battlespace,” said the commander of Group 13, who uses the callsign “Thirteenth.”
“What we are seeing in Crimea is exactly the fight UFORCE was built for. The Magura isn’t just a one-way-attack naval strike drone, it’s crossing hundreds of kilometers of open water and putting aerial drones on targets inland,” said Oleg Rogynskyy, chief executive of UFORCE. “That’s long-range strike effect at a fraction of what high-end systems cost. And nothing about it is specific to the Black Sea. Any contested waters, same logic. The future is battle-proven systems that work together and give operators options no single platform can.”
UFORCE said the operation showcases the same capability the Pentagon is now soliciting. The Defense Innovation Unit opened its Suitable Warfighting Adaptive Payloads (SWAP-USV) challenge in late July, offering $100 million in prize money for mature unmanned surface vessels integrated with at least two market-ready aerial drones able to detect and strike targets, with a Sprint 1 submission deadline of Aug. 10 and a further $200 million budgeted for follow-on production contracts. UFORCE has separately signed a memorandum of understanding with Alaska-based RECONCRAFT to build Magura vessels in the United States.
UFORCE’s release describes Magura’s hull as modified with hatches that open at sea, letting onboard FPV drones launch and fly toward nearby targets rather than being flown from shore, extending their range and reducing the time they spend exposed to jamming.
The company says it consolidated nine Ukrainian defense-technology developers, including the teams behind Magura and its Nemesis strike drone line, which includes a Magura-launched variant called SEASTRIKE. UFORCE’s statement did not specify whether Nemesis or SEASTRIKE, rather than the FPV drones GUR described, were the aircraft used in the Crimea strikes.

Germany: Berlin techno fans pause for Pride attack victims
Published August 15, 2026last updated August 15, 2026
What you need to know
This blog has closed. Below is a roundup of the top headlines from and about Germany on August 15, 2026:
- Russia adds Germany's Research Centre for East European Studies (FSO) to its list of 'undesirable' organizations
- A techno parade in Berlin takes place under heightened security following last month's deadly attack during a Pride march
- Johannes Liebmann breaks the world record in the men's 1,500m freestyle at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris
Don't let the algorithm hide the news. If you rely on our team for trusted reporting, please take a moment to select us as your Preferred Source on Google so you'll always see our verified news first.
For coverage of the wildfire in western Germany, head over to our dedicated blog here.
Germany's Weber clinches another European javelin gold
Germany's Julian Weber has won European Championship gold in the javelin throw for the second time.
The 31-year-old overcame shoulder issues to finish ahead of his teammate Nick Thumm with his final throw of 90.40 meters.
"I just wanted to show that I'm a mental beast. I’m so glad it worked out. I’m incredibly happy," Weber told ZDF public television.
Four years ago, he also secured a javelin gold at the European Championships in Munich.
Germany now sits third in the medal table with four golds, behind Italy and the United Kingdom.
On Friday, German sprinter Owen Ansah won the 200-meter final despite facing a potential ban from the National Anti-Doping Agency of Germany for allegedly failing to comply with a doping test.
Germany's Johannes Liebmann breaks world record in men's 1,500m freestyle
German teenager Johannes Liebmann set a new world record in the men's 1,500 meter freestyle with a time of 14 minutes, 26.79 seconds at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris.
Liebmann, who is 19 years old, beat the previous record of 14 minutes, 30.67 seconds, that had been held by American Bobby Finke since the 2024 Olympics.
Liebmann set out a cracking pace from the very beginning, with spectators cheering him on to the finish line over the final 200 meters.
Hungary's Zalan Sarkany won the silver medal, and Liebmann's teammate Oliver Klemet won the bronze medal.
Liebmann, who was taking part in his first European Championships, won the 800-meter freestyle earlier this week too.
President calls for end to fear after Berlin Pride attack
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier has urged society to protect the LGBTQ+ community against attacks like the van ramming and stabbing near the Berlin Pride parade three weeks ago.
On July 25, an Islamist attacker drove a van into a crowd and then allegedly attacked people with a machete, killing a woman and injuring at least 31 people.
"In an open society, everyone must be able to follow their own path," Steinmeier wrote in an article for the Zeit Online website.
This right applies "not only without fear, but also with pride; not only in private, but also in public," he asserted.
"Everyone has the right to self-determination, particularly where it concerns the very core of every human being — the expression of one's own personality, love and partnership, physicality and sexuality," the head of state continued.
Steinmeier said the attack primarily targeted queer people, leaving many afraid.
He stressed that a robust democracy cannot tolerate this and must prioritize law enforcement, public safety and education.
The head of state made the comments as several smaller German cities held their own Pride events this weekend, including Darmstadt, Bayreuth, Krefeld and Münster.
Berlin's Rave the Planet techno event starts with moment of silence
As tens of thousands of partiers gathered for "Rave the Planet" — a Berlin music event labeling itself a political demonstration — there was quiet before organizers began blasting music.
The now high-security event began with a moment of silence for the victims of an Islamist attack on an LGBTQ+ pride event at the same spot three weeks ago.
Taking place under the motto "imagine love," Rave the Planet is the first major party event in the German capital since the July 25 terror attack.
A Christopher Street Day (CSD) organizer invited to Saturday's event called on those gathered to "be courageous" … "especially now."
A large police presence is on hand to protect revelers, streets and paths have been closed and trams will not stop at regular destinations as a result of the event.
Rhine water levels fall again
Water levels on the Rhine River have fallen to new record lows, greatly disrupting river-borne cargo transport, as a prolonged dry spell continues in most of Germany.
According to the inland navigation agency WSV, the water level gauge at the Kaub bottleneck near Koblenz fell to 6 centimeters (2.4 inches) late on Friday and was 8 cm early on Saturday.
Until this year, the previous lowest level marked by the gauge was 25 cm recorded in 2018.
The gauge gives the depth over an arbitrary baseline near the bank of the river, but is an indication of the navigable depth at that point, which is around a meter (3 feet) deeper.
Most cargo previously transported on the Rhine has been shifted to road and rail, but these transport methods cannot fully compensate for the heavy loads carried by ships.
For this reason, companies have started to report disruption to their supplies, with chemical producers, utilities, steelmakers warning of higher costs, transport bottlenecks and reduced production.
Bonn authorities warn of potential danger after ordnance find
Authorities in the western city of Bonn have called on people to avoid an area of the Rhine riverbank in the Gronau district after ordnance was found there.
They said they would provide more information on any evacuation measures and street closures as it became available.
The ordnance was found not far from DW's Bonn headquarters, meaning that any evacuation order could also affect the international broadcaster.
The danger level has so far been described as "slight."
Potentially toxic algae spread in Germany's north
Health authorities have issued warnings to bathers as potentially toxic blue-green algae thrive in waters in the north of Germany.
When high concentrations occur in water, the algae can cause allergic reactions and irritation to skin and mucous membranes, and nausea and vomiting if ingested in sufficient quantities.
Satellite images from the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency show large patches of the algae — which are, in fact, cyanobacteria — in the Baltic Sea off the coast between Rostock and Hiddensee island, extending across the sea to the Danish coast.
They have also been found in lakes in the state of Schleswig-Holstein. Swimming in them has been banned until, probably, Wednesday.
The government in the state of Mecklenburg-Vorpomerania has warned against swimming in the sea when bathers can no longer see their feet in knee-high water.
AfD politician allegedly attacks 14-year-old — reports
A politician from the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is being investigated over an alleged attack on a 14-year-old boy found defacing one of the party's campaign posters, the Spiegel newsmagazine and other media have reported.
The incident in the city of Stendal occurred just weeks before an election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.
The Spiegel cited the State Criminal Police Office (LKA) as saying that the boy, along with other youths, was caught in the act of damaging an AfD poster.
"Subsequently, there was a possible physical altercation between a person with immunity and the youths. In the course of this, a blunt instrument was allegedly used," the LKA is quoted as saying.
It said one of the youths was slightly injured and received medical treatment.
Spiegel cited sources close to the boy as saying he suffered slight concussion, several bruises and injuries to his lip.
The public-service broadcaster MDR said the "blunt instrument" concerned was a baseball bat.
Heightened security planned at Berlin techno parade
The techno parade Rave the Planet is expected to draw tens of thousands of people in Berlin in Saturday, with police stepping up security at the event after last month's Islamist attack on fringes of the Pride march in the capital.
Participants in the parade will also have to contend with high temperatures of up to 37 C (98.6 F).
Police say they will deploy at least one water cannon to spray a cooling water mist and free drinking water is to be made available along the route of the parade, organizers have said.
The parade is to start in the early afternoon and run until late in the evening.
It is planned to run along the main boulevard through the Tiergarten park, between the Brandenburg Gate and the Victory Column, close to the site of the July 25 attack, in which an Islamist assailant killed a woman and injured at least 31 people, some seriously.
A police spokeswoman said some 1,500 officers would be deployed at the event, with Berlin police supported by colleagues from the states of Brandenburg and Saxony-Anhalt.
The techno parade was first held in Berlin in 2022 to celebrate electronic music culture and has taken place every year since then.
Organizers have registered 300,000 participants, though police have put the number closer to 100,000 at previous parades.
Russia lists another German research body as 'undesirable'
On Friday, Russia's Justice Ministry added the Research Centre for East European Studies (FSO), based at the University of Bremen, to its list of "undesirable" organizations
Such organizations are banned from carrying out activities within Russia's territory.
The public prosecutor's office claims that the FSO aims to lobby the US government to impose sanctions on Russia for its invasion of Ukraine.
According to the research institute's website, it is "a place where the Eastern Bloc and its societies, with their specific cultures, are studied, and where current developments in the post-Soviet region are analyzed."
Russia's list of "undesirable" organizations already contains several German ones, including Deutsche Welle (DW), the German Historical Institute (DHI), which has been active in Moscow for many years, the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) and numerous political foundations.

Ukraine Attacked the Savasleika Airfield, Where MiG-31Ks—Carriers of Kinzhal Missiles—Are Stationed
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:57:59 UTC
16:57:59 KST

The Ukrainian Armed Forces attacked the Savasleika military airfield in Russia’s Nizhny Novgorod region, where MiG-31Ks—carriers of Kinzhal aeroballistic missiles—are stationed.
A video of the fire at the airfield was published by the Telegram channel Exilenova+.
The attack on the airfield took place on the morning of August 15. In local chat rooms, residents reported explosions and began asking where exactly the explosion had occurred.
The Savasleika airfield is a Russian military airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region, located approximately 12 km northwest of the city of Kulebaki. The base houses a branch of the Russian Ministry of Defense’s 4th Centre for Combat Employment and Retraining of Personnel of the Aerospace Forces. The site is located approximately 650–700 km from the Ukrainian border, at coordinates 55.44199965223542, 42.30844483849896.
The airfield is home to various modifications of the MiG-31 fighter jet, including the MiG-31K, which carries the Kh-47M2 Kinzhal missiles.
This is not the first time the airfield has been targeted. In particular, on August 14, 2024, drones attacked Savasleika. At that time, local sources reported numerous explosions on the airbase grounds.
It later emerged that the strike targeted warehouses and fueling stations on the airfield grounds, around which traces of explosions were observed.

New excavations at Göbeklitepe unearth rectangular structures
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:55:11 UTC
16:55:11 KST

The use of public buildings and dwellings indicates that Göbeklitepe was not only a center for ritual activities but also a settlement where people lived. (AA photo)
Excavations in a new area of Göbeklitepe, a UNESCO World Heritage Site often described as the “zero point in history,” have uncovered rectangular structures dating to the site’s second phase of settlement.
Professor Necmi Karul, coordinator of the Taş Tepeler Project and head of the Göbeklitepe excavations, told state-run Anadolu Agency that excavations had begun this season in a new area north of the main excavation zone as part of the Culture and Tourism Ministry’s Legacy for the Future Project.
Karul explained that after moving the olive trees that once grew there, archaeologists were able to open up a 1,500-square-meter area for dig work.
He said the team aims to reassess and explore the potential of Göbeklitepe’s previously uncovered structures while continuing its approach of excavating broad areas and gradually going deeper over time.
“We started from one side of the area. As we moved north, we uncovered rectangular structures dating to Göbeklitepe’s second phase, immediately beneath the surface,” Karul said.
“The fact that they were just below the surface allowed us to quickly obtain evidence that gives us an idea about their plan and settlement layout. We even reached the floors of some structures very quickly,” he added.
Karul explained that the area is exposed to erosion and that the upper sections of the walls had been worn away over a long period.
He also said the olive trees had not caused significant damage to the structures. However, he noted that the area would probably have remained inaccessible to archaeologists had the trees not been relocated.
“Our plan this year is to remove the surface layer across the entire area and expose the remains of structures immediately below it,” he said.
Karul explained that the walking path around the new excavation site was designed so visitors can get an up-close look at the ongoing work and recent discoveries.
He noted that similar rectangular structures had previously been found in an area known as GT1.
“We are talking about their counterparts. But from what we have seen so far, we can say that the tradition of the standing stones had weakened and that these structures contained fewer standing stones,” Karul said.
“Looking at the interior arrangement of the spaces, they may have been used more for residential purposes. But, of course, it is not enough to say this simply by exposing the walls,” he added.
Karul said soil samples collected from inside the structures would provide further information about their functions, particularly once the excavation reaches floor levels.
“Our first impression is that they were used as dwellings,” he said.
Karul noted that previous excavations at Göbeklitepe had revealed both public buildings and contemporary residential structures.
The simultaneous use of public buildings and dwellings indicates that Göbeklitepe was not only a center for ritual activities but also a settlement where people lived, he said. Similar settlement patterns have also been identified at other excavation sites within the Stone Hills project.
Karul added that excavations were continuing particularly in the hillside area containing round structures.
According to him, reinforcement efforts shifted from Structure C, largely completed last year, to Structure D this year, with completion expected by the end of the year.

US says 19 million recalled eggs pose deadly risk
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:55:00 UTC
16:55:00 KST

US says 19 million recalled eggs pose deadly risk
- The FDA has classified 19 million eggs recalled by Midwest Poultry Services as a Class 1 risk due to potential salmonella contamination that can cause serious illness or death.
- The eggs were produced in Texas between June 6 and July 3, 2026, and sold across six states, including Texas and Oklahoma.
- Consumers are urged to not eat the eggs and to discard or return them for a refund; no illnesses have been reported so far according to the company.
AI generated
WASHINGTON - The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has said some 19 million eggs that were voluntarily recalled pose a reasonable risk of serious health consequences, including death.
Midwest Poultry Services voluntarily recalled the eggs over potential contamination with salmonella enteritidis on July 22.
The bacteria is linked to sometimes fatal infections, especially in young children, the elderly and people with weakened immunity.
On Aug 12, the FDA designated the recall category as Class 1, meaning “a situation in which there is a reasonable probability that the use of or exposure to a violative product will cause serious adverse health consequences or death.”
The eggs were produced in Texas between June 6 and July 3, 2026, with sell by or best by dates between July 20 and Aug 17, 2026.
They were distributed to stores and retail consumers in Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana, New Mexico, and Mississippi.
In all, 1,589,577 dozen eggs were covered by the recall, and included both white shell eggs and brown cage free shell eggs under a variety of brand names.
The company said it “identified the issue on two of its farm locations in Texas through proactive environmental monitoring practices and a robust internal investigation. The company also initiated its own testing protocols to identify potential sources of” salmonella.
“Do not consume the eggs. You should throw your eggs away or return them to your retailer for a full refund.”
It added it was not aware of any specific illnesses linked to its products. AFP

Artifacts from ancient Syrna site protected with landscaping work
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:54:59 UTC
16:54:59 KST

A protective barrier, landscaping and bilingual information signs in Turkish and English now safeguard the area containing the artifacts. (AA photo)
Architectural remains belonging to the ancient city of Syrna, dating to the Hellenistic period, have been placed under protection with landscaping work in the Marmaris district of Muğla.
Work was carried out in the village square of Bayır neighborhood to protect the historical artifacts and better introduce them to visitors.
As part of the project, supported by the Marmaris Chamber of Commerce, the area containing the artifacts was landscaped and a protective barrier was installed.
Information signs in Turkish and English detailing the historical and archaeological features of the artifacts were also placed at the site.
Among the protected artifacts is an ancient inscription containing important information about Syrna’s social and religious life.
The inscription records donations made for the sanctuary and altar of Asclepius, as well as contributions from different individuals and groups, in drachmas.
The records indicate the presence of the cult of Asclepius, the god of health and healing, in the region during antiquity and show that people from different segments of society contributed to the construction of the sanctuary.
The project also protected stepped pyramidal bases said to be unique to the Bozburun Peninsula, an altar with a snake relief associated with the cult of Asclepius, rusticated blocks and various fragments of bases.
The Marmaris Museum Directorate and Marmaris Municipality contributed to the project, along with Associate Professor Mehmet Gürbüzer, head of excavations at the ancient city of Amos and the project’s scientific adviser and his team.

How does a restaurant become a legend over 60 years?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:54:38 UTC
16:54:38 KST

Da Vittorio
In July in Bergamo, I joined Da Vittorio’s 60th anniversary celebration as a guest of the Cerea family. It felt less like a restaurant birthday party and more like a grand family reunion of the global gastronomic community. Nearly a thousand guests were spread across the lush grounds of Cantalupa, with 40 different food stations, chef friends arriving from around the world to cook, alongside producers and gastronomes. Ducks were being prepared in one corner, squid was coming off the grill in another, while bomboloni were frying elsewhere. Yet what made the evening truly remarkable was not so much what we ate, but who was there — and why.
Because when you looked at that crowd, you could actually see what Da Vittorio had built over six decades. They had not simply created a highly successful restaurant; they had built a gastronomic ecosystem in which producers, chefs, employees, friends and new generations were all connected. Perhaps this is precisely where the difference begins between restaurants that endure and those that simply come and go. Good restaurants make food; the ones that leave a mark create a culture around themselves in which new things can continue to grow.
The story begins in 1960, when Bruna Gioconda Gritti and Vittorio Cerea met at Caffè Orobica in Bergamo. Three years later, they married and began dreaming of opening a restaurant of their own. The opportunity came when they took over the former Ristorante Roma, then on the verge of bankruptcy. On 6 April 1966, Da Vittorio opened its doors. Yet Vittorio’s real courage lay not in opening a restaurant, but in the kind of restaurant he chose to open in Bergamo.
In a landlocked city where meat dominated the table, he placed fish at the heart of his cuisine. It may sound unremarkable today, but in 1960s Bergamo this was a serious gamble. As prosperity increased and fish, once considered a luxury, became more accessible, Vittorio recognised the shift early. He established a daily supply system to bring high-quality seafood into the city. That decision shaped the restaurant’s identity. The first Michelin star arrived in 1978, the second in 1996. In 2005, the family moved from the city center to the Cantalupa hills in Brusaporto; in 2010 came the third Michelin star.
But to me, what makes Da Vittorio truly iconic has less to do with its stars than with something else: The fact that people travel to a three-Michelin-starred restaurant for a plate of tomato pasta.
Paccheri alla Vittorio is now the restaurant’s signature dish. The large tubular pasta is coated in a velvety sauce in which the sweetness, acidity and intensity of different tomato varieties are carefully balanced; Parmesan and butter provide the finishing touch. There is no ostentatious luxury ingredient. No caviar, no truffle. The technique does not shout for attention. In the end, what sits in front of you is still pasta with tomato sauce. But it is made with such precision that it has become as powerful a part of the restaurant’s identity as its logo. Paccheri has reportedly been on the menu since the 1980s, and Da Vittorio is said to prepare around 50,000 portions a year at events outside the restaurant.
Yet the Cerea family did not stop at that one iconic plate. Today, the second generation carries the business forward across different areas: Chicco and Bobo in the kitchen, Rossella overseeing hospitality, Francesco working across catering, events and consultancy. Through the Da Vittorio Academy, they pass their knowledge on to younger generations; the training goes beyond recipes to encompass markets, production regions, ingredients and technique. In other words, the knowledge once accumulated inside Vittorio and Bruna’s small restaurant has evolved into a structure capable of educating others.
That was what moved me most on the night of the 60th anniversary. Vittorio Cerea is no longer alive, yet the story he and Bruna began in 1966 continues to grow. And it is being carried forward not only by their children, but by the people they have trained, the producers they have worked with and the relationships they have built across the world.
Restaurants that endure are not simply those that cook well; they are the ones that add something to gastronomy. A great plate can make someone happy for an evening. A strong culture, however, can give rise to new chefs, new producers, new collaborations and new stories.
Where to stay
If you ask me where to stay in Milan, my recommendation is the Excelsior Hotel Gallia, directly opposite Milano Centrale. At first glance, its location may seem to be simply a matter of convenience, but it is in fact an important part of the hotel’s story. Opened in 1932, the Gallia belongs to the era when travelling by train was itself a form of luxury and grand railway hotels were among Europe’s most prestigious addresses. Today, behind its historic façade, it has been transformed into a hotel that brings together Milan’s past and its contemporary design culture.
Italian architect Marco Piva led the major renovation. A new glass-and-steel wing was added alongside the historic building, placing old and new side by side, while inside you encounter some of the most important names in Italian design, including Poltrona Frau and Cassina. The hotel also houses more than 500 works of art. At Gallia, design is not merely decoration; it is an integral part of the experience.
On the top floor, Terrazza Gallia is led by Executive Chef Vincenzo Lebano, who, together with Chef de Cuisine Andrea Calia di Dio, interprets the traditions of different Italian regions through a contemporary lens. What makes it especially interesting is that the restaurant’s gastronomic direction is shaped through a collaboration with the Cerea family of three-Michelin-starred Da Vittorio. So here, once again, you encounter an extension of the story that began in Bergamo, this time reaching into Milan.
And Terrazza Gallia should not be thought of only as a dinner destination. Overlooking the monumental façade of Milano Centrale and the city skyline, the terrace is particularly enjoyable for an aperitivo at sunset. Breakfast, too, deserves special mention. Alongside the classic five-star hotel buffet, Gallia Restaurant offers a distinct “Epicurean Breakfast” concept. You can begin with a proper espresso or cappuccino and move on to artisanal pastries, cheeses and charcuterie and omelettes prepared to order. To me, this is where a luxury hotel’s gastronomic credentials are truly tested; good food should not exist only on white-tablecloth tables in the evening, but should extend through the entire day, from the coffee you drink in the morning to the eggs on your breakfast plate.
That is exactly why I like Gallia. This is not simply a five-star hotel where you sleep in a beautiful room. It brings together three of Milan’s greatest strengths under one roof: History, design and gastronomy. In the morning, you step outside and find yourself in the middle of the city’s rush; in the evening, you look down on that same city from the terrace, aperitivo in hand. For a few days in Milan, it is difficult to imagine a better starting point.

Kandilli tracking sunspots by hand for 79 years
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:54:28 UTC
16:54:28 KST

A researcher records solar activity by mapping sunspots by hand.
Researchers from Istanbul’s Boğaziçi University have recorded sunspots by hand every day since 1947, a research institute official has said at an astronomy gathering in the western province of Afyonkarahisar.
The Scientific and Technical Research Council of Türkiye (TÜBİTAK) Sky Observation Event hosted hundreds of enthusiasts at Emre Lake for daytime solar monitoring and nighttime viewings of the Perseid meteor shower.
Institute lecturer Cihan Tuğrul Tezcan said they are pleased with visitor interest during their first attendance at the gathering. Fatih Gökmen established the observatory in 1920, starting observations with a 20-centimeter telescope, he said.
Continuous monitoring began in 1947 by projecting the sun’s image directly on paper to mark surface spots, Tezcan said.
“We keep these daily records, identify and number the spots and send them to international data centers to study the evolutionary structures, processes and activity periods,” he said.
International observatories still utilize this traditional method to ensure permanent data retention in both physical and digital archives, Tezcan said.
The filterless technique utilizing direct white light yields higher resolution data through the optical system’s diffraction limit compared to modern cameras requiring protective filters to preserve eye health and equipment lifespan, he said.
Observers normally must settle for limited camera resolution, but this manual method yields healthier and much more precise data, Tezcan said.
Located in Istanbul, Kandilli Observatory operates as Türkiye’s primary institution for seismology and astronomical research. TÜBİTAK regularly organizes observation events across various provinces to popularize space sciences for the public.

Facade overhaul revamps city’s historic peninsula
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:54:19 UTC
16:54:19 KST

A restored corner building stands on a busy avenue in Istanbul’s Fatih.
Municipal teams launched a sweeping facade rehabilitation project targeting 92 buildings along major commercial avenues in Istanbul’s Fatih district to strip away visual pollution and restore civil architecture.
The overhaul on Fevzipaşa and Macar Kardeşler avenues spans the Akşemsettin, İskenderpaşa, Ali Kuşçu and Zeyrek neighborhoods. Crews are dismantling unregulated extensions like air conditioning units, antennas, cables and oversized signs while repainting structures using a designated color palette.
To date, workers finalized restorations on 21 buildings, offering the service mostly free of charge to property owners.
“This is a very important commercial axis. We want to create a more organized, higher-quality avenue people enjoy walking and shopping in,” Fatih Mayor Mehmet Ergün Turan said.
The municipality’s Preservation Implementation and Inspection Bureau drives the evaluations. When necessary, scientific committees and preservation boards join the multidisciplinary process utilizing historical visual and technical data.
Turan said civil architecture examples represent vital components of cultural memory. He noted past municipal interventions rehabilitated nearly 1,000 buildings in the Fener and Balat neighborhoods, driving a huge tourist influx. Teams later overhauled about 200 buildings on Büyük Karaman Avenue.
“We are removing attachments like air conditioners and antennas from buildings on Fevzipaşa Avenue. We leave signs only on ground floors, which we will standardize later,” he said.
Local tradesman Serkan Şahin said the restoration lifted a heavy burden off property owners while changing the avenue’s momentum.
Istanbul’s Fatih district constitutes the city’s historic peninsula, housing former Byzantine and Ottoman imperial capitals. The area faces strict zoning regulations to preserve its UNESCO-recognized heritage, requiring extensive coordination for structural modifications.

Tavşan Island’s coral model heads to COP31
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:54:09 UTC
16:54:09 KST

A general view of the uninhabited Tavşan Island, part of the Princes’ Islands in the Marmara Sea.
A pioneering 11-year marine conservation and coral restoration initiative from Tavşan Island in the Marmara Sea is set to take center stage at the COP31 climate summit in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya.
Accompanied by Marine Life Conservation Society (DYKD) Chairman Volkan Narcı, Istanbul Governor Davut Gül and Zero Waste Foundation President Samed Ağırbaş toured the conservation site.
Located off Istanbul’s coast in the Princes’ Islands, the uninhabited island, also known as Neandros, is a third-degree archaeological site closed to unauthorized entry. DYKD biologist Ulaşcan Kayataş noted that this natural isolation makes it an ideal testing ground free from human pressure.
Teams have restored over 700 gorgonian coral colonies since 2015, achieving an 80 percent survival rate for yellow gorgonians. Divers launched a new program in January 2026 to strengthen purple coral (Paramuricea clavata) populations, marking a first for Türkiye.
Kayataş said the program detected naturally multiplying juvenile corals. Operating with an integrated conservation approach, the society continues to monitor fish species, octopuses and seagrasses.
Crews removed 650,000 square meters of ghost nets and 3 tons of lead from the seabed, recycling some nets into agricultural covers and bags to contribute to the circular economy.
“When human pressure is removed and pollution stops, nature somehow renews itself,” Gül said, calling nongovernmental organization support for state initiatives extremely valuable.
“We want to turn targets into field applications and applications into measurable results,” Ağırbaş said, noting that the initiative proves how conservation, restoration and continuous monitoring operate together.
The foundation combats plastic pollution in the Mediterranean and Aegean seas, Ağırbaş said, calling the issue a crucial problem for human health and the environment.
Calling the 11-year restoration zone a pilot region for the climate summit, Narcı said, “At COP in Antalya, we will tell the world this: Türkiye has created a model demonstrating its 30x30 targets by actively implementing them in the field.”
Partnering with the Antalya Governor’s Office, the DYKD will roll out the project’s next phase off Üç Adalar, Tekirova and Çıralı, collaborating with local stakeholders to map key habitats and inventory the marine ecosystem.
As the host of the COP31 UN climate summit, Türkiye will hold the main event in the southern province of Antalya from Nov. 9 to 20.

Türkiye’s railway network has expanded by nearly 3,000 kilometers since the Justice and Development Party (AKP) came to power in 2002, Transport and Infrastructure Minister Abdulkadir Uraloğlu has said.
The network grew from 10,948 kilometers to 13,919 kilometers over the period, while 2,251 kilometers of high-speed railway were built from scratch, Uraloğlu said.
The minister said the existing network had also been renewed and modernized. Signaling systems now cover 61 percent of railway lines, while more than half have been electrified.
Türkiye has become the sixth country in Europe and eighth worldwide to operate high-speed trains, which have carried 114 million passengers since services began in 2009, according to Uraloğlu.

Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:52:02 UTC
16:52:02 KST

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said Iran’s economic problems have sharply worsened since its war with the US and Israel.
He said during a meeting that rising prices are driven by higher import costs and falling state revenues caused by reduced oil sales, according to Iranian media.
Pezeshkian says imported goods once entered Iran through more direct routes, but now take longer and more expensive routes, pushing up prices.
He also underlined that declining oil sales have cut government revenues, with Iran unable to sell oil at previous levels.
"Our income has also decreased. We used to sell oil, now we can't," Pezeshkian said.
Damage to industrial facilities has added to the economic strain, the Iranian leader noted, as many factories were hit and destroyed during the Israel-US attacks.
Pezeshkian noted that the damage has also reduced tax revenues, leaving the government struggling to collect payments from affected factories.
"We can't collect taxes from factories, and not only that, we have to give them money so they can stay afloat," the Iranian president said.
“Our problems have worsened dramatically, while our income has declined,” Pezehskian said.
Israel-US war on Iran
US and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran on February 28, 2026, killing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and targeting leadership, military and infrastructure sites.
Iran retaliated with missiles and drones against Israel, US bases and regional targets, with Iranian authorities reporting more than 3,500 deaths.
Iran severely disrupted the Strait of Hormuz, choking a major global oil route and reducing shipping to a trickle for months.
The disruption triggered a historic oil-supply shock, pushing Brent above $100 a barrel at times and sharply raising shipping and insurance costs.
The crisis disrupted global trade, increased inflation pressures and raised concerns over slower economic growth worldwide.

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Saturday said the freedom secured through decades of sacrifice carried with it a responsibility to preserve it and ensure that its gains make India prosperous, secure and capable of contributing to the world, as the organisation marked the 80th Independence Day at events in Nagpur.Hoisting the Tricolour at the RSS headquarters in Nagpur, Bhagwat said Independence Day was both an occasion for celebration and remembrance.“Independence Day is a subject of pride and celebration for all of us. Man, 18, pleads guilty to repeatedly kicking sea lion in California
Ishani Desai
- Tyler Muehl, 18, pleaded guilty to repeatedly kicking a sea lion in San Diego, violating the Marine Mammal Protection Act and facing prison and fines.
- The incident happened during sea lions' mating season, causing distress to the animals and drawing criticism from wildlife advocates.
- Experts urge the public to keep distance from sea lions to prevent harm to both animals and people, recommending a 45m safe space.
AI generated
SAN DIEGO, California - An 18-year-old man bobbed from side to side on his toes near a roaring beach in San Diego and kicked a sea lion’s chin, causing the animal to recoil.
It scampered away on a concrete barrier but the man raised his hands, poised as if ready for a boxing match, and lobbed another kick at the sea lion’s hindquarters, according to a video of the July 22 episode that was posted on social media and gained widespread attention.
The man, Tyler Muehl, pleaded guilty on Aug 13 in federal court in San Diego to violating the Marine Mammal Protection Act, which prohibits harassing or hunting oceanic animals.
He faces a year in prison and a US$100,000 (S$127,960) fine when he is sentenced Oct 26, the authorities said.
Robyn Davidoff, chair of the Sierra Club’s San Diego Seal Society chapter, said she had seen tourists throw rocks at pups, touch sea lions, creep close to snap pictures of them and block them from slipping into the ocean.
But she has never seen in La Jolla – a neighbourhood in San Diego known for beautiful beaches, seaside cliffs and marine wildlife – a case where a sea lion was kicked.
“When we see something like this, an intentional and repeated harassment, it’s hard to comprehend,” she said.
Muehl admitted he kicked the sea lion four times near the Ellen Browning Scripps Park and chased the animal. He referred to himself as a professional mixed boxer, the authorities said in a news release.
He only ended his pursuit when the sea lion heaved itself over a concrete barrier and flopped onto a beach, the authorities said.
Kelly Thorton, a spokesperson for the US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California, declined to disclose Muehl’s motive in the attack.
Dana Grimes, Muehl’s lawyer, said in an e-mail that her client is a teenager who quickly accepted responsibility. “We will present all of the mitigating circumstances at the appropriate time in court,” she said.
Mother sea lions often come ashore to give birth around La Jolla. Muehl’s actions happened during the animals’ mating season, Davidoff said.
Davidoff and her organisation work to educate the public about sea lions. “Don’t approach them, don’t touch them, don’t feed them,” she said.
Rob DiGiovanni, the executive director and chief scientist for the Atlantic Marine Conservation Society, said federal law recommends staying 45m away from marine animals.
Sea lions can weigh anywhere from 135 to 270kg he said, and people can be seriously injured if they provoke one.
“Why do we need to stress them out?” he said. NYTIMES

Prime office rents in Istanbul climbed to a record 52 dollars per square meter per month in the second quarter of 2026, up 13 percent from a year earlier in dollar terms, according to a new report.
Cushman & Wakefield TR International’s Türkiye MarketBeat Half Year 2026 report attributed the rise to limited prime office supply, low vacancy rates in the central business district and sustained demand for well-connected, high-quality buildings.
In lira terms, prime rents reached 2,359 liras per square meter per month, an annual increase of 32.6 percent.
Levent-Etiler recorded the highest rate at 52 dollars, followed by Maslak at 40 dollars.
Prime rents stood at 35 dollars in Esentepe-Gayrettepe-Zincirlikuyu and on the Asian side, 25 dollars in Ankara and 22 dollars in İzmir.
New leases in Istanbul’s Grade A office market totaled 86,202 square meters in the first half of the year, rising 57 percent from the same period of 2025.
The market has recovered from the pandemic-era shift to remote work, while limited development and the conversion of some offices to housing have reduced the supply of modern, centrally located space.

Malaysia’s Anwar vows to boost anti-corruption drive after state poll defeats
The prime minister says the country’s economic data is ‘not winning the hearts of the people’ but adds ‘reforms cannot be rushed’
Anwar acknowledged shortcomings by his administration that had led to frustration among Malaysians. While the economy grew 6 per cent last quarter and unemployment was low, Anwar said he “won’t deny” that Malaysians faced higher living costs.
“The economic numbers are not winning the hearts of the people,” Anwar said at the annual congress of his People’s Justice Party, or PKR. “I know some people are demanding, but reforms cannot be rushed, it has to be done in stages” and must take into account other parties in the ruling coalition, he said.
PKR and the Pakatan Harapan coalition led by Anwar have fared poorly in three consecutive state elections in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan. The party lost control of Negeri Sembilan this month, going from holding the chief minister’s office to just two seats in the 36-seat assembly. Barisan Nasional, Anwar’s federal government partner and electoral rival, and its allies won supermajorities in Johor and Negeri Sembilan at Pakatan’s expense.
“The message of the people has been clear” following losses in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, Anwar said in Malacca state, which is due to hold its local election by January.
Anwar, 79, who was earlier reported to be considering calling a snap general election as soon as October this year, has indicated he is not in a rush to go to the polls after the recent setbacks. The national poll is due by February 2028.

Ukraine strike hits Russia’s main space rocket maker
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:46:57 UTC
16:46:57 KST

- Russian officials confirmed a missile strike on an industrial facility in Samara overnight Aug. 15, without naming the target.
- Ukrainian open-source analysts identified the likely target as Building 106A of the Progress rocket-space center.
Ukrainian long-range strikes hit an industrial site in Samara, Russia, overnight into Aug. 15, triggering a regional air raid alert and a series of explosions residents reported hearing across the city, according to Russian officials and Ukrainian open-source monitoring of the aftermath.
Samara region governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev confirmed that a missile struck an industrial enterprise in the region, saying emergency services and an operational headquarters were on site and that details on casualties were still being clarified. He did not name the facility. Samara Mayor Ivan Noskov later said a “massed attack” by enemy missiles caused localized damage to the city’s industrial infrastructure, adding that Russian air defenses had intercepted part of the attack. Neither official specified how many missiles were involved or which weapon system struck the ground.
The Ukrainian open-source analysis group CyberBoroshno, which has previously published satellite-imagery assessments of Flamingo missile strikes inside Russia, said the strike most likely used a Ukrainian FP-5 “Flamingo” cruise missile and identified the impact point as Building 106A at the Progress facility, geolocating it to coordinates 53.217623, 50.303163.
Ukrainian commentator Oleh Ponomar separately reported the same conclusion, citing the group’s “GEOINT collective” analysis. Neither Ukraine’s military nor Progress itself had publicly confirmed the specific building as of this writing, and the claim rests on CyberBoroshno’s imagery review rather than official acknowledgment from either government.
According to CyberBoroshno’s assessment, Building 106A is part of the production complex for the Soyuz launch vehicle family and operates as a cleanroom facility, where onboard electrical systems, instruments and circuit boards are installed. The group described the building’s function as producing the rocket’s guidance and control systems, cable network and instrument compartment, work that must be completed before a rocket can be considered finished even after its airframe and fuel tanks are built. CyberBoroshno said a neighboring structure, Building 106B, serves as the final assembly point for completed rockets and may also have been damaged by the blast.
Progress, formerly known as TsSKB-Progress, has produced Soviet and Russian launch vehicles since the 1950s, including the R-7-derived rocket that carried Yuri Gagarin into orbit in 1961. It is Russia’s only facility that performs series production of the Soyuz-2 family of launch vehicles, used both for crewed and uncrewed missions and for placing military and commercial satellites into orbit. The plant also builds electro-optical reconnaissance and Earth-observation satellites.
CyberBoroshno said the facility’s significance lies in that exclusivity. The group said Soyuz-2 rockets built at Progress launch and replenish Russia’s military satellite constellations, including the Liana network used for signals intelligence and targeting and the Persona and Razdan optical reconnaissance satellites, as well as the Rassvet broadband satellite constellation operated by Bureau 1440, a Russian company building a domestic answer to Starlink. Public launch records reviewed independently show that Bureau 1440’s Rassvet satellites, including test and commercial batches launched in 2023 and again in March and July 2026, have so far flown exclusively aboard Soyuz-2.1b rockets from the Vostochny and Plesetsk cosmodromes, a pattern consistent with CyberBoroshno’s characterization, though it could not be independently confirmed that no other launch vehicle has ever been used or is planned.
CyberBoroshno assessed that recovery from fire and firefighting water inside a cleanroom facility would take considerably longer than a conventional industrial repair. The group said restoring the site would require reclassifying clean-room zones, recertifying the manufacturing process and re-testing for airborne particulate contamination, work it estimated in months rather than weeks. The group also said Soyuz onboard electronics depend on imported components subject to export restrictions that Russia cannot currently readily replace, though it did not provide further detail on which specific components would be affected.
The FP-5 Flamingo, built by the Ukrainian company Fire Point, is a ground-launched cruise missile with a published range of up to 3,000 km (1,860 miles) and a warhead of roughly 1,000 to 1,150 kg (2,200 to 2,540 pounds). Ukraine first used the missile in combat in August 2025 against a Russian security service facility in Crimea, according to Ukrainian officials at the time. Fire Point told the Associated Press in 2025 that it aimed to raise production from an initial 30 units a month to 210 units a month by October of that year, though independent verification of actual output has remained limited. CyberBoroshno has previously attributed Flamingo strikes to attacks on the VNIIR-Progress electronics plant in Cheboksary, a separate facility from the Samara center that manufactures satellite-navigation receivers and antennas, and on the Antipinsky oil refinery in Tyumen in July.
The scale of damage at the Samara site remains unresolved.

Powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Indonesia, killing at least 40
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:46:18 UTC
16:46:18 KST

A second 6.9-magnitude quake later hit Pematangsiantar on the western island of Sumatra, at a depth of around 183 km. The first quake hit at a depth of around 10 km.
A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake hit the Southeast Asian nation of Indonesia on Saturday, killing at least 40 people.
The quake struck to the north of Flores Island in the eastern part of the country in the early hours of the morning, sparking panic as people fled into the streets amid crumbling buildings.
A tsunami warning was issued but was later lifted, with Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysical Agency (BMKG) saying it was no longer detecting significant sea level rises that could threaten coastal communities.
Fathur Rahman, a rescue official, said the death toll had risen to 40 on Saturday evening, with 50 people also injured.
According to the National Agency for Disaster Countermeasure (BNPB), 2,000 people in the Nagekeo Regency self-evacuated after the quake.
Nelly Florida Riama, a deputy director for geophysics at BMKG, earlier warned that while the tsunami warning was over, aftershocks were "still occurring."
"We urge the public to remain calm, not to be swayed by irresponsible rumours, and to keep up to date with information from the BMKG’s official channels,” Nelly added.
The BNPB said tremors were reported to have been felt across the regencies of Nagekeo, Sikka, and West Manggarai in the province of East Nusa Tenggara; Bima City and Bima Regency in West Nusa Tenggara; and in the Jeneponto, Selayar Islands, and Maros Regencies in South Sulawesi.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has expressed her condolences to families affected by the quake and said the EU was ready to deploy its Copernicus Earth observation satellites to assist.
"From solidarity to action, Europe stands ready to deploy Copernicus, our eyes in the sky, to support search and rescue efforts," she wrote in a post on X.
A second 6.9-magnitude earthquake later hit Pematangsiantar on the western island of Sumatra, at a depth of around 183 km. The first quake hit at a depth of around 10 km.
Earthquakes that occur at greater depth tend to cause less destruction than those closer to the surface, as the strength of shaking reduces with increasing distance from its source.
Authorities are assessing the impact of the second quake.

Gallery: Ukrainian children's fairytale art from Kharkiv reaches Estonia
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:46:00 UTC
16:46:00 KST

Gallery: Ukrainian children's fairytale art from Kharkiv reaches Estonia
More than a dozen works by young artists in Kharkiv are now on display in Pärnu, blending forgotten legends and untold tales with new mythologies in large, colorful scenes.
"Lost Fairy Tales" opened at the Pärnu Museum of New Art (MONA) this week, showcasing 14 monumental original works created by about 40 children and teens ages 5–17.
Kharkiv's Aza Nizi Maza art studio continues to operate from a World War II-era bomb shelter, where kids still meet, learn and create amid ongoing drone, missile and guided-bomb strikes on the city.
The exhibition grew from the idea of a "missing museum" — a world made up of forgotten legends, untold stories and new mythologies inspired by the Baroque collections of European museums.
The young artists first drew elements found in ancient frescoes, botanical atlases, medieval maps and manuscripts before developing characters and building narratives around them.
Details like rosehips, seashells, bones, bats, lions and musical instruments meet characters ranging from beggars, saints and witches to princesses, children and those who have seen it all.
The scale of the works, which measure 2.5 x 1.5 meters, allows viewers to step into these visual worlds and become part of the unfolding narratives.
Curated by Mykola Kolomiiets and Iryna Hrytska, "Lost Fairy Tales" will remain on view in Pärnu through October 4.

====================================================================================================

this milan apartment is bursting with thousands of twentieth-century masterpieces
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:45:15 UTC
16:45:15 KST

It’s a bit difficult to find the entrance to Casa Museo Boschi Di Stefano because it’s not housed in a traditional ‘museum.’ Located in the Porta Venezia neighborhood of Milan, there is no grand museum entrance. Instead, you find it by entering one of the towering palazzos, or apartment buildings. It’s one of several of Milan’s ‘house museums,’ former residences that have been transformed to hold vast collections of art and antiquities, opening historic homes up to public view. What makes the former home of Antonio Boschi and Marieda Di Stefano special is its vast collection of twentieth-century art. In their lifetime, the socialite couple rubbed shoulders with famous artists and designers of the period, accumulating about 2,000 pieces from friends and icons alike. What results is a domestic space that holds both the memory of the family and the century alike.
in Milan, the former home of the former home of Antonio Boschi and Marieda Di Stefano now displays their collection of twentieth-century art | all images courtesy of Casa Museo Boschi Di Stefano
Antonio Boschi, Marieda Di Stefano, and their cats
The entrance to their former apartment is on the second floor of a building designed by Italian architect Piero Portaluppi between 1929 and 1931. It’s an older building reminiscent of a bygone era for Milan—the floors are mosaic tiles formed in a triangular pattern, and a spiraling staircase running the circumference of the building’s interior leads you to the entrance. The walls are a trompe l’oeil of painted stone. The building was commissioned by Marieda Di Stefano’s father, who envisioned the multistory building as a series of units for his children to live in side by side.
Greeting visitors in the entrance hall of their former residence are two paintings of the couple: I coniugi Boschi (1951) and I coniugi Boschi (1947), which roughly translates to The Boschi couple, or Mr. and Mrs. Boschi. They are half-length portraits of the pair holding their cats, created four years apart by the painter Remo Brindisi. The Italian painter himself has his own house museum dedicated to his works outside of Bologna, designed by the famed Italian architect Nanda Vigo.
view of a guest room in the residence housing paintings like Arturo Tosi’s Songavazzo (1925) and Achille Funi’s Trieste (1933) among others
Donated to the Municipality of Milan
The couple was deeply situated in the Milanese community. Antonio Boschi was a longtime engineer for the high-end tire manufacturer Pirelli, known for its involvement in Formula 1 racing. Marieda Di Stefano studied ceramics and continued to practice her passion throughout her lifetime, with a few of her pieces displayed in the house. Upon their passing, their collections were entrusted to the Municipality of Milan. The collection would be exhibited at Palazzo Reale in 1974 while a more permanent exhibition space was sought.
the entrance to the house museum with a view of ceramic plates created by Marieda Boschi Di Stefano
The House before it was a museum
After some renovations, the former home of the couple was modified to accommodate the works. The house museum at Via Giorgio Jan, 15, which is beautiful, pristine, and filled with filtered natural light, was not the state of the house while it was being lived in. The couple stored a huge collection in this space. It was so vast that the entirety couldn’t possibly fit on the available wall space.
Photographs taken by Gabriele Basilico in 1982 create a kind of faithful capture of how the home would have looked when occupied by Boschi and Di Stefano. This series was commissioned by Italian Radical design figure and Domus editor Alessandro Mendini (who was also Marieda Di Stefano’s grandson). The floors were covered in a patchwork of what looks to be Persian carpets. There were huge canvases stacked upon each other and leaning against the wall. There were framed paintings puzzle-pieced together to take advantage of all the vertical surfaces that existed between floor and ceiling.
in 1982, a series of photos of the home was commissioned by Italian Radical design figure and Domus editor Alessandro Mendini (who was also Marieda Di Stefano’s grandson)
Touring the twentieth century in eleven rooms
Now, the space’s eleven rooms are arranged to take the visitor chronologically and thematically through the 20th century of art: ‘from the Novecento Italiano to Mario Sironi, from the painters of Corrente, Giorgio Morandi and Filippo De Pisis to the so-called School of Paris and the Chiaristi, from Lucio Fontana to Spazialismo and Informale.’ Although many of the works are from Italian artists, there is a section from English artist Ralph Rumney, who was a member of the avant-garde Situationist International movement in Europe. In a room of Giorgio de Chirico works, one can find The School of Gladiators: The Combat (1928). And finally, there are the famed Concetto spaziale works of Lucio Fontana, the infamous slashes through canvas that he became known for.
After making your way through a fairly ordinary apartment made extraordinary by just a sliver of the couple’s collection, there’s a sense of awe at the many functions a house could have: shelter, a meeting ground, a museum, a treasure chest for artistic marvels.
before the museum officially opened in 2003, the couple kept huge canvases stacked upon each other and leaning against the wall as their collection was too big fit on their walls
designed by Piero Portaluppi, the building was commissioned by Marieda Di Stefano’s father, who envisioned the multistory building as a series of units for his children to live in side by side

The plant in Samara was hit by Flamingo – confirmation has emerged
Kyiv • UNN
Explosions rang out in Samara on the night of August 15. Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point confirmed the strike on the missile center.
During the night of August 15, 2026, a series of explosions rang out in Samara, Russia. OSINT analysts said that the area where the Progress Rocket and Space Center and the Aviakor aircraft plant are located was hit. Ukrainian weapons manufacturer Fire Point confirmed that the Progress rocket center was hit, UNN reports.
The Progress Rocket and Space Center is one of the key enterprises in Russia’s rocket and space industry. The center develops and manufactures medium-class launch vehicles, including the Soyuz-2 family, as well as spacecraft for remote sensing of the Earth and scientific programs.
According to preliminary data, the strike hit the enterprise’s main assembly shop. A threat to a building located next to the Aviakor aircraft plant, which repairs and services Tu-95MS strategic bombers, was also reported.
As the CyberBoroshno OSINT channel indicates, this likely refers to Building 106A.
It is part of the Soyuz launch vehicle production complex. Building 106A operates under a high cleanroom standard: onboard electrical equipment, instruments, and printed circuit boards are assembled here—in effect, the launch vehicle’s “nervous system”: the control system, cable network, and instrument compartment. Without this stage, the rocket cannot be assembled, even when the body and tanks are ready.
The authorities of the Samara region confirmed that an industrial facility had been hit. At the same time, they said that the attack had been repelled. An operational headquarters was established in the region.
Denys Shtilerman, chief designer and co-founder of Fire Point, also published a video of a missile launch, apparently the same one that hit the space manufacturing facility in Samara.

'Broken and grateful': Alice Springs farewells Kumanjayi Little Baby
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-15
07:42:27 UTC
16:42:27 KST

IN BRIEF
- Almost four months after the death of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby, the community has gathered for her funeral service.
- The Warlpiri girl has been described as a beautiful "little princess" who loved cuddling puppies, the colour pink and music.
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the name and image of an Indigenous person who has passed away.
This article may be distressing to some readers.
Alice Springs is known as the Red Centre of Australia but on 15 August, the community donned pink for the funeral of five-year-old Warlpiri girl, Kumanjayi Little Baby.
Warlpiri Elder and family spokesperson Robin Granites said pink was her favourite colour — it "reminds us of the clothes she used to wear".
"And the times when we would go in the evening, you see the sunset and even the early morning, you see the pink colour of clouds and that ... is a really good colour for us," Granites said ahead of the funeral.
News that makes sense
Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.
Kumanjayi Little Baby's body was found on 30 April, after she went missing from Old Timers town camp, south of Alice Springs. Her disappearance sparked a five-day search, described as one of the largest search efforts in Northern Territory history.
47-year-old Jefferson Lewis has since been charged with her alleged murder and two other offences that cannot be published for legal reasons.
Pastor Rejeili Paulo-Smith spoke on behalf of Kumanjayi Little Baby's mother at the funeral service.
She requested that her daughter be remembered, "for who she was, not simply for the tragedy of how her life ended".
"Kumanjayi wasn't simply a little girl who was known by the community. She was Mum's baby too. She was a little girl whose presence filled their home and whose absence has left an enormous space," Paulo-Smith said.
Jintangka: 'We're all in one'
It's been almost four months since the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby. During this time, her family and Indigenous communities have engaged in the grieving period and mourning process known as Sorry Business.
In recent months, Paulo-Smith said the community had felt "both broken and grateful".
"Broken because a precious little life has been taken from us far too soon, yet grateful because Kumanjayi Little Baby was here. She was known, she was loved, she mattered," she said.
The week following Kumanjayi Little Baby's death, thousands of Australians gathered at nationwide candlelight vigils.
At a local vigil in Alice Springs, 89-year-old Maya Cifali told NITV News the outpouring of community spirit was unlike anything she had ever seen.
"It is the first time that such a community spirit is felt for all of us," Cifali said.
She has lived in Alice Springs for around 40 years.
Granites also believes the local community has displayed the Warlpiri concept of Jintangka; "which means we're all in one, everyone together".
At the funeral, he took the opportunity to thank Australians and people overseas for rallying behind his family during and in the months following the search for Kumanjayi Little Baby.
"That really helped us during those sad days, those unforgettable days," Granites said.
"We've done everything we can to help each other, so we should be all proud of each other and say thank you."
A memorial service was held for Kumanjayi Little Baby on 14 August.
Following public funeral proceedings on 15 August, there was also an intimate burial service.
'Forever five, forever young'
Liberal senator and Kumanjayi Little Baby's family member Jacinta Nampajinpa Price was in attendance at the funeral.
SBS News can confirm Minister for Indigenous Australians Malarndirri McCarthy, Sue-Anne Hunter, the National Commissioner for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children and Young People and Katie Kiss, the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Social Justice Commissioner, attended the funeral.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese previously visited Alice Springs, where he described Kumanjayi Little Baby as a "cherished" child and offered his condolences to her grieving family.
"It's important to be able to say to the family that the nation stands with them in their grief," Albanese said in May.
There was a sombre atmosphere at Kumanjayi Little Baby's funeral, with speeches punctuated by cries from the crowd. Hundreds of people visited to pay their respects, with attendees spilling beyond the funeral Chapel and onto the grass lawn.
Kumanjayi Little Baby was remembered as a "beautiful", "loved" and "treasured" child who brought joy to her family. She loved rainbows, the colour pink, music and cuddling puppies.
She was described as her mother's "little princess", who will be remembered as "forever five, forever young".
Speaking on behalf of Kumanjayi Little Baby's mother, Paulo-Smith said, "Kumanjayi's earthly life was short, but her life was not without meaning".
"As Mum has said, we look to the night sky and remember the brightest star. Not because the star replaces you but because it reminds us to lift our eyes beyond what we can see."
